result.text:
Quoted commas in `POST /import` now import correctly. The full suite passes with 104 of 104 tests, and `src/legacy/` and `package.json` are unchanged.

**Cause:** `parseLegacyCsv` in `src/legacy/csvImport.ts` splits each line on every comma, so `"Müller, Hans"` became two cells and every later column moved by one.

**Fix:** I didn't touch `src/legacy/`, because the Monday sync would overwrite any change there. Instead:
- `src/lib/csv.ts` (new) has a quote-aware parser, `parseShipmentCsv`. It gives the same output as the legacy one for unquoted rows and reuses `mapLegacyCarrier` from `src/legacy/carrierCodes.ts`.
- `src/routes/import.ts` now calls the new parser instead of the legacy one.

The new parser also accepts `""` as an escaped quote and line breaks inside quoted fields. A multi-line quoted field counts as one record, so the `line` numbers in import errors then refer to the record, not the physical line.

**Tests:** `test/csv.test.ts` is new. It covers the splitter, a row with `"Müller, Hans"` (all columns land correctly), unquoted rows, empty input, and a full `POST /import` request with a quoted comma. My first test number had a wrong check digit and the ATP validation rejected it; I corrected the test data, and the parser was fine.

The legacy parser still has the bug. `test/import.test.ts` still imports it, but nothing else in the app does. You may want to tell the platform team so they can fix it upstream and the copy in `src/lib/csv.ts` can go.
